newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - July 23.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
* In an effort to save money in the Medicare program, President Clinton vowed to defend lawmakers who support raising premiums on the affluent elderly.
* Ruth Messinger, candidate for mayor of New York City, outlined more than $1 billion in reductions in the city budget to cover her proposed spending program.

* The profits from a business using deaf Mexicans to sell trinkets on New York subways allowed the family of Jose Paoletti Moreda to rise from its lower-middle-class roots in Mexico to buy homes in New York and Los Angeles as well as a fleet of vehicles.
* Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan suggested that the central bank was inclined to leave interest rates steady for the time being.
* Russia's President Boris Yeltsin vetoed legislation that would have curbed religious freedom, but could face an override vote.

* Switzerland's major banks are publishig a list Wednesday of roughly 2,000 dormant World-War-II-era accounts that may include assets of Holocaust victims, naming more than twice the number of such accounts the banks said they had identified earlier.
* American officials hope that winning the return of two suspects in San Diego for trial in Mexico will encourage Mexican officials to honor more American extradition requests.
